articles.title: The edge AI wall: Why embodied AI requires new mathematics
articles.summary: The article argues that embodied AI systems such as autonomous mobile robots, humanoids, delivery robots, and self-driving vehicles face an “edge AI wall” when heavy AI models are moved from cloud environments onto battery-powered physical platforms. The bottleneck is both physical, driven by energy, heat, weight, and latency constraints, and mathematical, driven by combinatorial explosion as real-world decision spaces become more complex.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is useful for framing why robotics and embodied AI may not scale like cloud AI. It highlights potential investment bottlenecks around onboard compute, batteries, thermal management, and real-time planning, while also suggesting that future progress may depend on new architectures or mathematical approaches rather than simply adding more GPUs.
